title: TCGCSV-first variant expansion (schema + algorithm rework, full reset)
description:
Take TCGCSV as the authoritative source for which printings a card has, instead of bootstrapping from pokemontcg.io price keys + rarity heuristics. Audit showed 130+ fabricated reverse_holo printings in ASC alone and BLK cards with non-existent 'normal' printings.

Bigger goal (added per user feedback): no conditional logic in the application to compensate for a bad data model or shitty data. The right answer is to make the data right and let the SQL queries be straightforward.

Schema changes (edit V1 directly — user has authorized a full wipe, no migration history to preserve):
1. New tcgcsv_products table: (product_id PK, group_id, name, collector_number, derived_variant). Populated by import_tcgcsv so expansion can query the full product list without holding it in memory.
2. printings gets a sub_type_name column. Set at expansion time from the TCGplayer sub_type the variant maps to. Price queries then become a simple JOIN — no CASE expressions, no IS NULL OR fallbacks.

Algorithm:
- import_tcgcsv runs BEFORE variant expansion and persists products + prices.
- derive_variants_from_tcgcsv(card): for the card's set group + collector number, list TCGCSV products. For each base product, emit one printing per advertised sub_type (Normal → normal, Reverse Holofoil → reverse_holo, Holofoil → holo, ...). For each pattern product (Master Ball / Energy Symbol / etc.), emit one printing of that pattern variant. Each printing knows its product_id and its sub_type_name.
- expand_all_printings: TCGCSV-derived first; if a card has no TCGCSV products (brand-new set TCGCSV hasn't fetched), fall back to a minimal 'just normal' bootstrap. Layer-3 overlay still applies on top for true exceptions (stamps, manual additions).

Code to delete:
- VARIANT_PRICE_SUBTYPE CASE constant (no longer needed once printings carry sub_type_name).
- IS NULL OR sub_type filter pattern at each call site.
- bootstrap_from_rarity's release_date pre-LC reverse-holo check (TCGCSV tells us what exists, not the year).
- variant_from_product_name + auto-create logic in link_card_printings — gets pulled into the new derive step.

Process:
1. V1 migration: add tcgcsv_products, add sub_type_name to printings.
2. Implement derive_variants_from_tcgcsv + new expand_all_printings.
3. Reorder data.rs refresh: TCGCSV first, then expand.
4. Simplify all price subqueries.
5. Tests: ASC patterns (Energy Symbol/Quick Ball); ASC C/U/R that should NOT get plain RH; BLK with no Normal sub_type; pre-LC commons; overlay still wins.
6. Teardown prod volume + reseed; spot-check ASC Dreepy, BLK Klink, 151 Bulbasaur, WHT Swadloon, base1 commons.
close_reason: Closed

title: Antique Cover Fossil (zsv10pt5-80) misplaced + /card 404 due to upstream number='60'
description:
Reproduction: http://192.168.1.93:8090/browse/zsv10pt5?page=7 shows card "Antique Cover Fossil" with collector number 80 wedged between #60 (Escavalier) and #61 (Klink) on the lower-left of the binder grid. http://192.168.1.93:8090/card/zsv10pt5/80 returns 404 (\`/api/card/zsv10pt5/80\` → HTTP 404). \`/api/card/zsv10pt5/60\` returns Escavalier, masking Antique Cover Fossil entirely.

Root cause (upstream, not us): pokemontcg.io's row for \`zsv10pt5-80\` has \`id: "zsv10pt5-80"\` and image URL \`https://images.pokemontcg.io/zsv10pt5/80.png\` (both correctly say "80") but \`number: "60"\`. Verified live against \`https://api.pokemontcg.io/v2/cards/zsv10pt5-80\` on 2026-05-25 — not a stale cache; a \`pkdump data refresh\` will not help.

Why the symptoms: \`get_card_detail\` in \`crates/pkdump-db/src/cards.rs:130\` looks up cards by \`WHERE set_code = ?1 AND c.number = ?2\`, so any caller passing "80" finds nothing while "60" returns the first matching row (Escavalier).

Scope: this is the ONLY upstream row in the entire shared catalog with this kind of \`card_id\` ↔ \`number\` disagreement. Verified via:
\`\`\`sql
SELECT card_id, set_code, number, substr(card_id, length(set_code) + 2) AS suffix
  FROM cards
 WHERE raw_json IS NOT NULL
   AND substr(card_id, length(set_code) + 2) != number
   AND substr(card_id, length(set_code) + 2) NOT LIKE '%\\_%' ESCAPE '\\';
-- → 1 row: zsv10pt5-80 / 60 / 80
\`\`\`
(The \`cel25c-N_A\` Classic-Collection rows are intentional multi-printing disambiguators and are excluded.)
design:
Two plausible approaches; user to pick.

**A. Explicit override seed file (recommended).** Add \`data/overrides/upstream_card_corrections.json\`, list of \`{ card_id, set?: ..., number?: ..., ... }\` entries. After upstream cards are ingested, a final phase applies the overrides. First entry: \`{ "card_id": "zsv10pt5-80", "number": "80" }\`. Matches the existing pattern of \`data/overrides/variant_augmentations.json\` and CLAUDE.md's "data IS the product" guidance. The override file becomes the registry of known upstream-data corrections — easy to extend.

**B. Card-id suffix heal.** At ingest, when the trailing segment after \`set_code-\` is pure digits and disagrees with upstream \`number\`, overwrite \`number\` to match the id suffix. One-line fix, but introduces an implicit rule. Today this would only affect zsv10pt5-80, but it'd silently auto-correct any future similar upstream rows without leaving a paper trail.

Both: same fail-first test (currently passing) — a row exists for \`zsv10pt5-80\` with \`number = '80'\`, \`get_card_detail("zsv10pt5", "80")\` returns the card, binder query for page 7 places it in slot 80.
acceptance_criteria:
- \`/api/card/zsv10pt5/80\` returns Antique Cover Fossil (not 404).
- \`/browse/zsv10pt5?page=7\` places Antique Cover Fossil in slot 80, not adjacent to Escavalier in slot 60.
- A test reproducing the wrong placement / 404 was added in the same commit as the fix (fail-first).
- No regression in any other set's binder placement.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bridge TTBB groups into variant expansion (cross-group source allowlist)
description:
Extend variant expansion in \`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs\` so Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle products attach as variants of their parent cards.

**Change.** Add the three TTBB TCGplayer group IDs to \`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\` (currently \`[2374, 1840]\`). \`preload_cross_group_products\` already keys by normalized collector_number; for every TTBB product whose \`collector_number\` resolves to a base card in another set, expansion will pick it up automatically.

Group IDs:
- 3179  — Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (2022)
- 23266 — Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle 2023
- 23561 — Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle 2024

**Variant codes.** Whatever pokedumpster-vz2 concludes — at minimum \`cosmos_holo\` for the 10 TTBB24 products that already carry \`derived_variant = 'cosmos_holo'\`. Additional codes may be needed for 2022/2023/2024 plain reprints depending on the research.

**Resolution path.** TTBB products come in two name shapes that need to dispatch differently:
1. \`"Darkrai (Cosmos Holo) 136/197"\` — parenthetical pattern, \`derived_variant\` already populated by tcgcsv ingest. Existing pattern-overlay resolution in \`preload_cross_group_products\` handles these.
2. \`"Phantump 016/196"\` — bare name (no parenthetical). Today this shape only resolves via the Deck Exclusives path (\`DECK_EXCLUSIVES_GROUP_ID\`), which uses \`prices.sub_type_name\` to pick a variant. TTBB doesn't fit that model. Likely needs a new resolution branch: "bare-name product in a TTBB group → attach with the year-specific variant code". Implement that branch only for years where vz2 says a distinct variant is needed.

**Test.** Add fail-first integration tests modeled on \`cross_group_cosmos_holo_attaches_to_numbered_set_card\` and \`cross_group_deck_exclusive_non_foil_attaches_to_base_card\`:
- One for a TTBB24 Cosmos Holo product attaching to its parent.
- One per year where a new variant code is introduced.

**Re-ingest.** After landing, run \`pkdump data refresh\` (or \`deploy/seed.sh prod\` if local catalog is stale) so existing TTBB products become printings.
acceptance_criteria:
- \`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\` includes 3179, 23266, 23561.
- TTBB24 Cosmos Holo products show up as variants on their parent card pages.
- All TTBB products that ought to attach (per vz2 disposition) have at least one matching \`printings\` row.
- Fail-first integration tests demonstrate at least the Cosmos Holo path and any new variant code paths.
- No regressions in existing MCAP/Deck-Exclusives expansion tests.

title: Research TTBB variant codes (2022/2023/2024) before ingest bridge lands
description:
Blocking the TTBB ingest extension. Before we add the three TTBB groups to \`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\` we need to know what variant code each TTBB product should attach as, because that determines whether they become duplicates of the parent printing or a distinct variant chip.

Open TCGplayer (or images.pokemontcg.io if it has them) and inspect sample products from each group:

- **TTBB 2022 (group 3179, 30 products, all \`derived_variant IS NULL\`):** Sample products: 283766 "Gengar (2021 Copyright Date) 057/198", 283785 "Mewtwo 056/172", 283790 "Chandelure 033/192". Question: do these carry a 2022 Halloween jack-o'-lantern stamp/marking, or are they bare reprints visually identical to the parent set's non-foil? If stamped → new variant code (proposal: \`ttbb_2022\`, label "Trick or Trade 2022", short tag "TTBB22"). If identical → don't bridge these products at all (they'd just duplicate the parent printing).
- **TTBB 2023 (group 23266, 30 products, all \`derived_variant IS NULL\`):** Sample products: 515647 "Phantump 016/196", 515654 "Pikachu 062/193", 515661 "Gengar (2022 Copyright Date) 066/196". Same question for 2023.
- **TTBB 2024 (group 23561, mix):** 10 products tagged \`cosmos_holo\` (already a known variant). 20 products with no derived_variant. Cosmos Holo: should just work once the group is bridged. Plain products: same question — stamped/distinct or bare reprint?

For any year where a new variant code is needed, add a row to \`data/variants.json\` (label, short tag, sort rank, chip color). For Halloween stamps, propose chip color in the orange/purple family.

Note: \`cosmos_holo\` already exists in \`data/variants.json\` and the tcgcsv ingest already parses it for TTBB24 products. Confirm but no schema work needed there.

Output of this task: an answer per year (bridge-as-variant with code X / bridge-as-duplicate-skip / don't bridge) recorded as notes on the parent decision pokedumpster-gnh.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the three TTBB years has a documented disposition: variant code + label, or "skip" with reason.
- \`data/variants.json\` updated for any newly-needed codes.
- pokedumpster-gnh updated with the conclusion (--notes).

title: How to surface Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (TTBB) cards
description:
TCGCSV exposes three Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle groups — TTBB (group 3179, 2022, 30 products), TTBB23 (23266, 2023, 30 products), TTBB24 (23561, 2024, 30 products). pokemontcg.io has no matching set rows for any of them, and none of our \`sets\` map their \`tcgcsv_group_id\` at them. As a result the /browse page never lists them, and zero \`printings\` reference any TTBB product ID — even though each TTBB product carries a collector_number that resolves to a real card in another set.

User decision (2026-05-25, owner: ryan): **variants-primary**, with a secondary logical-set entry-path view.

Rationale: every TTBB product is numbered for a card that exists in some other set (e.g. TTBB23 "Phantump 016/196" → Lost Origin 016; TTBB24 "Darkrai (Cosmos Holo) 136/197" → Paldea Evolved 136). The physical card is the same Pokémon at the same collector number — sometimes with a TTBB-exclusive finish (Cosmos Holo in 2024) or a Halloween stamp (need to verify 2022/2023). So the canonical model is: extend variant expansion to attach TTBB products to their parent cards, with appropriate variant codes. A logical-set view is added on top purely as a data-entry affordance so the user can input a whole TTBB pack from one page instead of navigating to 30 individual cards.
design:
**Variant attachment.** Extend the cross-group bridge in \`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs\` (\`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\`, currently \`[2374, 1840]\`) to also include the three TTBB group IDs: \`3179, 23266, 23561\`. \`preload_cross_group_products\` already keys by normalized collector_number, so resolution falls out for free once the groups are in the allowlist — every TTBB product whose \`collector_number\` matches a card in a real pokemontcg.io set will be picked up and become a printing of that card.

**Variant codes (needs research before code):**
- TTBB 2024 Cosmos Holo: \`derived_variant = 'cosmos_holo'\` is already populated for these by tcgcsv ingest. The \`cosmos_holo\` variant code already exists in data/variants.json. Should just work.
- TTBB 2024 plain (no parenthetical, e.g. "Sprigatito - 012/193"): need to confirm whether these are visually identical to the parent set printing or carry a TTBB-exclusive marking (Halloween stamp etc.). If identical → don't attach (it's a duplicate of the parent). If distinct → introduce a \`ttbb_2024\` or similar variant code.
- TTBB 2023 plain reprints (group 23266, all 30 products have \`derived_variant IS NULL\`): same question — confirm whether they carry a 2023 Halloween stamp or are bare reprints. Likely need a \`ttbb_2023\` variant code with a Halloween stamp label.
- TTBB 2022 plain reprints (group 3179, mostly bare-name): same — likely \`ttbb_2022\` with a stamp label.

Open the TCGplayer product pages for a few sample products from each group; check the card image for distinguishing marks before deciding.

**Logical-set view (secondary).** Do NOT seed real rows in the \`sets\` table for TTBB. Instead add a /ttbb (or /sets/ttbb) route that, given a TTBB group_id, lists the 30 products in collector_number order and renders each as a slot linking to the *parent card's* binder slot (with the TTBB variant preselected for the +1 affordance). This keeps the data model honest: TTBB has no set in pokemontcg.io, so it shouldn't synthesize one. The view is pure UI sugar over \`tcgcsv_products\` joined to \`printings\` via product_id.

The /browse page should still surface this view via a tile or sidebar entry ("Trick or Trade Bundles") so the user can find it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision recorded: variants-primary, with logical-set entry view as secondary affordance.
- TTBB variant-code question is researched (parent-identical vs. distinct stamp/finish) per year before any ingest code lands.
- Follow-up feature issue(s) created for: (1) extend cross-group bridge to TTBB groups + add any new variant codes; (2) logical-set entry view; (3) /browse surface for the entry view.

title: Normalize set symbol glyphs at ingest time
description:
Upstream pokemontcg.io symbol PNGs are not uniformly sized — PNG canvases range from 25x15 (POR/me2) to 38x38 (TWM/sv6) and contain varying amounts of transparent padding. The browse/+page.svelte tile uses height: 28px with width auto, so the rendered glyph size varies wildly across sets. Toggling to height: auto is worse.

Fix at the data layer: during catalog ingest, fetch each set's upstream symbol PNG, trim the alpha bbox, resize to a uniform target height (64px = 2x the 28px CSS size for retina crispness), and self-host under $PKDUMP_HOME/symbols/<set_code>.png. Rewrite sets.symbol_url to /sym/<set_code>.png. Add a new column symbol_source_url so 'pkdump data refresh' can detect when pokemontcg.io rotates a symbol and re-trim.

Server gains nest_service('/sym', ServeDir::new(data_dir.join('symbols'))) — analogous to the existing /sets route but data-volume-backed instead of image-baked. Override symbol_urls (/sets/mep-symbol.svg etc.) are left untouched: bridge file still wins.
design: Schema V3: ALTER TABLE sets ADD COLUMN symbol_source_url TEXT. Ingest module pkdump-ingest/src/symbols.rs::normalize_all_symbols(conn, data_dir). Idempotent: skips when symbol_source_url matches and the file exists. Fetch/decode errors log + skip + leave the row's URL untouched (best-effort enrichment, must not fail catalog refresh). Uses the 'image' crate for PNG decode/encode + Lanczos3 resize.
acceptance_criteria: 1) After pkdump setup, every set with an http(s) symbol_url has a corresponding file at $PKDUMP_HOME/symbols/<set_code>.png. 2) sets.symbol_url for those sets points at /sym/<set_code>.png. 3) Override symbol_urls (those starting with /) are untouched. 4) GET /sym/sv6.png returns the trimmed-and-normalized PNG. 5) On the /browse page, all set glyphs visibly render at the same height with no padding variance. 6) pkdump data refresh re-trims only when the upstream symbol_url has changed (symbol_source_url comparison).
close_reason: Implemented: ingest now trims alpha bbox + resizes upstream symbol PNGs to 64px height, self-hosts under $PKDUMP_HOME/symbols/, server adds /sym route, sets.symbol_url rewritten to local path. Verified on prod: 172 sets normalized, 2 overrides preserved (mep, svp), 0 failures.

title: MEP (Mega Evolution Promo) absent from /browse — synthesize sets rows for orphan TCGCSV promo groups
description:
TCGCSV has group 24451 'ME: Mega Evolution Promo' (abbreviation MEP, 83 products, published 2025-09-26), but our 'sets' table has no row for it. So MEP never appears in the browse selection, even though we already have the catalog data and pricing.

This is the same shape as SVP (TCGCSV group 22872 'SV: Scarlet & Violet Promo Cards'). SVP shows up in /browse only because pokemontcg.io has a 'svp' set entry (ptcgo_code PR-SV) — even with sets.tcgcsv_group_id NULL, the set still renders. MEP has no pokemontcg.io counterpart, so it has no sets row at all.

Two separate gaps revealed here:
1. pokemontcg.io has not published a 'Mega Evolution Promo' set (~8 months past release — beyond the usual 2–3 month upstream lag).
2. Our linker resolve_group_set_links in crates/pkdump-ingest/src/tcgcsv.rs:240-258 matches by ptcgo_code abbreviation then normalized set name. Even if pokemontcg.io adds MEP, the abbreviations almost certainly won't match (TCGCSV uses 'MEP', pokemontcg.io will likely use 'PR-ME' following the PR-SV / PR-SW / PR-SM pattern), and the normalized names won't match either ('SV: Scarlet & Violet Promo Cards' vs 'Scarlet & Violet Black Star Promos' is the existing precedent). So the auto-linker won't bridge MEP automatically once upstream catches up.
design:
Two options to evaluate:

Option A (lightweight, immediate): hand-bridge in an overrides file. Add data/overrides/tcgcsv_set_bridges.json mapping {tcgcsv_group_id -> set_code} OR {tcgcsv_abbreviation -> ptcgo_code}. The linker reads this overlay last, after the abbreviation+name auto-match. This also fixes SVP at the same time.

Option B (more general): synthesize a sets row for any TCGCSV group that survives the auto-link pass without a match and looks like a 'promo set' (abbreviation ends in 'P', or has 'Promo' in name, or 'Black Star' in name). Synthetic sets get a generated set_code (e.g. 'mep'), the TCGCSV group's name and published_on, and tcgcsv_group_id wired up. Risk: synthesizing creates rows that pokemontcg.io will eventually duplicate, leaving us with split data.

Recommend Option A: an explicit overlay is the canonical 'manual bridge' for ingest gaps in this codebase (see variant_augmentations.json — same pattern). Per CLAUDE.md, data, not logic.
acceptance_criteria:
- After running pkdump setup / data refresh: sets table has a row joined to TCGCSV group 24451 (MEP). Cards from MEP appear in browse.
- SVP gets a real tcgcsv_group_id link via the same mechanism (currently NULL despite having a sets row).
- Overrides file is small, readable, hand-maintained.

title: Variant expansion ignores TCGCSV group 1840 'Deck Exclusives' — drops non-foil deck-origin rares
description:
The variant expander in crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs scans only the card's own TCGCSV group plus one cross-group catch-all, hard-coded as MISC_GROUP_ID = 2374 (MCAP).

It does NOT scan group 1840 ('Deck Exclusives'), which is the canonical TCGCSV home for non-foil cards that ship inside preconstructed products (Build & Battle decks, theme decks, Battle Academies, etc.). Group 1840 currently holds 479 products spanning XY-era through current; 331 of them have a 'Normal' sub_type price entry. Every one of those is a real non-foil printing that PokeDumpster is silently dropping.

Concrete repro: I have a non-foil rare Zacian 045/094 from Phantasmal Flames (me2-45). TCGCSV product 664005 lives in group 1840 with sub_type 'Normal'. PokeDumpster has only me2-45-holo and me2-45-reverse_holo printings — no normal variant. The me2-45-normal printing should exist.
design:
Per CLAUDE.md 'data model is the product': the set of cross-group source groups should be data, not a Rust constant.

Two-step fix:

1. Replace MISC_GROUP_ID constant with a list of cross-group source group IDs. Could be a small static array in code for now; eventually a seed file alongside variants.json.

2. Extend preload_cross_group_products to scan group 1840 as well. Modern bare-name products in 1840 (e.g. 'Cinderace - 028/198', 'Zacian - 045/094') have no parenthetical pattern — they need a new resolution branch that defaults their sub_type-derived variant to 'normal' via sub_type_to_variant. Older 1840 products with parentheticals like (Cracked Ice Holo) / (XY Base Set) already route through variant_from_product_name.

Match logic for 1840 is the same as non-stamp MCAP overlays: collector_number normalize-match, plus card_name_lower + set_total disambiguation when set_keyword is absent (it always will be for plain 1840 entries).
acceptance_criteria:
- Fail-first test: card me2-45 with TCGCSV product 664005 in group 1840 (sub_type 'Normal') produces a me2-45-normal printing after expand_all_printings runs.
- Existing tests for group 2374 (MCAP) behavior still pass.
- After running 'pkdump data refresh' against a real catalog: me2-45-normal exists in printings; spot-check a handful of other modern bare-name 1840 entries (e.g. Cinderace - 028/198) also get normal printings on their base cards.
- No regressions on patterned 1840 products like Yveltal - 78/146 (Cracked Ice Holo) — those continue to resolve via the existing pattern parser.
notes: Investigation context: see conversation that produced this issue. The 331 'Normal' sub_type count in group 1840 is the upper bound on the number of new printings this will create across the whole catalog; the actual write count will be lower because some collector numbers won't have a matching pokemontcg.io card.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 678e487 — cross-group preload now scans group 1840 in addition to 2374, and uses sub_type_to_variant for bare-name products. Fail-first test covers Zacian PFL case + leak guard.

title: pkdump setup — variant expansion rate drops 3x past ~9000 cards
description: Live progress instrumentation revealed expand_all_printings throughput collapses from ~150 cards/s to ~55 cards/s once it gets past ~card 9000, and keeps degrading. The shared catalog connection only sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON — no WAL, no cache_size bump, no synchronous tuning. With the default ~2MB page cache, once the printings table + its indices exceed cache size every per-card UPDATE/INSERT round-trips to disk; default fsync-on-commit also serializes every per-card transaction. Fix: in open_shared(), set PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL + synchronous=NORMAL + cache_size=-65536 (64MB). Expected: cliff disappears, total expansion drops from ~370s to well under 100s.
close_reason: open_shared() now sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, cache_size=-65536 (64MB) — WAL keeps writes sequential, NORMAL drops the per-commit fsync (crash-safe in WAL), 64MB cache keeps the printings table + indices hot through the entire per-card transaction loop.

title: Attach MCAP non-stamp products (Cosmo Holo, etc.) to numbered-set base cards
description:
preload_stamp_products in crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs only matches MCAP (group 2374) products whose name parses as a stamp tag. Other treatments MCAP hosts — currently observed: Cosmo Holo — are silently dropped, so cards like Erika's Tangela in ME2.5 (#7, MCAP product 679253 'Erika's Tangela 007/217 Cosmo Holo') are missing their fourth variant.

The variants table already knows cosmos_holo; this is the ingest side.

title: Move variant display metadata into a shared.sqlite `variants` table
description: Variant display data (label, sort rank, chip color, short table tag) currently lives in four scattered TS/Svelte functions plus a Rust KNOWN_VARIANTS constant. Move all of it into a single shared.sqlite table seeded from data/variants.json at `pkdump setup` time. Add a FK from printings.variant so ingest can no longer silently introduce unknown codes.
design:
Schema:
- variants(code PK, label, short, rank, color) — all NOT NULL
- printings.variant becomes FK -> variants(code)

Source of truth: data/variants.json (flat list of {code,label,short,rank,color} records). pkdump setup re-seeds the table (DELETE + INSERT) so the file is authoritative.

API: GET /api/variants returns the full list. Frontend fetches once on first need and caches in a /variants.svelte.ts store; the four display functions collapse to map lookups.

Migrations:
- shared migration N: CREATE TABLE variants ... + seed (initial rows so the FK can be added)
- shared migration N+1: ALTER printings ADD constraint (or rebuild via temp table — SQLite has no direct ADD FK).

Removes the 'Rh → Reverse Holo' stopgap in variantLabel() since the label is now data.
close_reason: Implemented: V2 migration adds variants(code,label,short,rank,color) with FK from printings.variant; data/variants.json is the canonical seed; pkdump_db::variants::{reconcile,ensure_code,list_all} drive setup/ingest; /api/variants endpoint feeds a Svelte 5 $state store that replaces the four scattered TS heuristics (variantLabel/Rank/Color/Tag).

title: link_card_printings flattens multi-product-per-card pricing
description:
tcgcsv::link_card_printings runs UPDATE printings SET tcgplayer_product_id = ?1 WHERE card_id = ?2 — so all variants of a card end up pointing to the SAME TCGplayer product, whichever the linker processed last. TCGplayer actually has separate products per pattern (Holo vs Reverse Holo vs Poke Ball vs Master Ball vs Trainer Gallery), each with its own pricing. Today, pokeball_rh and masterball_rh printings for 151 / Prismatic Evolutions share the price (and the new card-detail price-history chart) of the base printing, not their actual market.

Fix scope:
1. Match TCGplayer products to a specific printing variant, not just to a card. TCGplayer's extendedData typically carries hints (e.g. 'Number' with a suffix, or product name containing 'Master Ball'). Need to parse those and route to the right printing_id.
2. Schema is already OK — printings.tcgplayer_product_id is per-printing — just the linker logic is too coarse.

title: Bogus reverse_holo printings on pre-Legendary-Collection sets (base1…base5)
description: Reverse holos didn't exist in the English Pokémon TCG until Legendary Collection (base6, 2002-05-24). But for Common/Uncommon/Rare cards in the original base, jungle, fossil, etc. sets, pokemontcg.io has no TCGplayer price-key block, so layer-1 expansion (variants_from_price_keys) yields nothing and layer-2 (bootstrap_from_rarity) kicks in. The bootstrap unconditionally adds 'reverse_holo' for those rarities, so the browse 'Add' modal shows a non-existent reverse-holo variant for, e.g., base1-58.\n\nFix: pass each card's set release_date into the expansion and have bootstrap_from_rarity skip reverse_holo when release_date < 2002-05-24. Threads through expand_variants → expand_all_printings (which already SELECTs from cards — just JOIN sets). Then re-run 'pkdump data refresh' on prod to soft-deprecate the wrong rows. Also filter deprecated printings out of the browse modal unless the user owns a copy, so existing wrong printings disappear from the UI.

title: Card-detail price history chart (time-series graph)
description:
Card-detail view currently shows only the latest market price per printing (CardDetailView.svelte 'Printings' table → Market column). User wants a time-series chart of price over time per printing.

title: Collection table: variant/status tags pushed to right edge when card name wraps
description:
On /collection, the .namecell is a flex row containing the thumbnail, the card name \`\`, and the inline variant + status tags (e.g. "R" for Reverse Holo, "H" for Holofoil). When the card name fits on a single line, the tags abut the right edge of the name — natural left-aligned cluster. When the name is long enough to wrap to two lines, the tags get pushed to the right edge of the cell instead of continuing to abut the name. Cause: in \`frontend/src/routes/collection/+page.svelte:1566\` (\`.namecell { display: flex; align-items: center; }\`) the cardname span is a flex sibling of the tags. When its content would overflow, default \`flex-shrink: 1\` shrinks the span to whatever width remains after \`thumb + tags + gaps\`, forcing the text to wrap. The shrunken width is, by construction, equal to "available width minus tags", so the tag siblings land at the right edge of the cell. Markup at \`frontend/src/routes/collection/+page.svelte:867-884\`: \`\`\`svelte
… {a.name} … …
\`\`\`
design:
Wrap the cardname + tags in a single inline child of the flex row. Inside that wrapper they flow as inline content — when the name wraps, the tags follow the last line naturally and stay glued to the name. \`\`\`svelte
… {a.name}{#if a.variant !== 'normal'}…{/if}{#if statusBadge(a.status)}…{/if}
\`\`\` CSS: \`.namebody { min-width: 0; }\` and ensure \`.tag\` is \`display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle\` so the small letter-tags keep their pill shape while flowing inline. Verify by widening "Antique Cover Fossil" or similar long-named entry in the browser at small viewport width and confirming tags abut the wrapped name, not the cell's right edge.
acceptance_criteria:
- For both single-line and wrapped card names, the variant/status tags appear immediately after the last word of the name (left-clustered with the name), not at the cell's right edge.
- No visual regression on the other \`.namecell\` usage (line 964 — no tags, thumb + cardname only).
- Verified in a running browser, not just a static read.
close_reason: Closed

title: upstream_card_corrections: re-apply override to already-ingested rows
description:
\`data/overrides/upstream_card_corrections.json\` is applied inside \`upsert_card\` (\`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/pokemon_tcg_data.rs\`). That covers any newly-ingested row, but adding a new entry today does NOT heal a row that's already in the catalog — \`pkdump data refresh\`'s \`import_tail\` skips sets that already exist (\`crates/pkdump-cli/src/data.rs:142\` — \`if exists { continue; }\`), so existing cards are never re-upserted on the nightly path.

Concrete: when pokedumpster-fxb landed, the \`zsv10pt5-80\` row had to be healed with a one-time SQL UPDATE on prod because \`pkdump data refresh\` did not re-run \`upsert_card\` against it. The override is correct for any future ingest of that card, but the existing row needed manual intervention.

This is fine when the registry has exactly one entry. It becomes annoying if corrections accumulate (or if a correction is edited later) because every change would require a manual heal in prod.
design:
Add \`pkdump data apply-corrections [--dry-run]\` to the CLI. Walks every entry in \`upstream_card_corrections.json\`, and for each \`card_id\` that already exists in the \`cards\` table, applies the field-level overrides via UPDATE (and recomputes \`number_sortable\` when \`number\` is overridden). Idempotent — re-running is a no-op once rows match. \`--dry-run\` prints the rows that would change without writing.

Where the code goes:
- New \`fn apply_corrections(args)\` in \`crates/pkdump-cli/src/data.rs\` next to the existing \`refresh\` entrypoint.
- Re-use the override loader from \`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/pokemon_tcg_data.rs\` — extract \`upstream_card_corrections()\` to a small \`pub fn\` if needed, or factor a tiny \`apply_corrections_to_db(conn) -> usize\` next to it that the CLI calls.
- The healing SQL mirrors what \`upsert_card\` writes: \`UPDATE cards SET number = ?, number_sortable = ?\` (using \`pkdump_core::number_sortable\` for the sortable value), \`raw_json\` left untouched per existing convention.

Optional but probably worth it: also call \`apply_corrections_to_db\` as a final phase of \`pkdump data refresh\` so the next nightly heals any row whose override was added between runs. Cost is one SELECT per override entry — negligible.

Fail-first test: insert a card row with the wrong field value, run \`apply_corrections_to_db\`, assert the field updated to the corrected value and \`number_sortable\` recomputed. A second run is a no-op.
acceptance_criteria:
- \`pkdump data apply-corrections\` exists, walks the override registry, UPDATEs every matching \`cards\` row.
- \`--dry-run\` reports planned changes without writing.
- Either the new subcommand runs as part of \`pkdump data refresh\`, or there's a clear operator note telling the user to run it after adding an override.
- Fail-first test covers: corrected field is applied; \`number_sortable\` follows; second run is a no-op; non-matching card_ids are skipped.
- pokedumpster-fxb's prod heal becomes reproducible: run the subcommand against any catalog and the \`zsv10pt5-80\` row converges to \`number='80'\`.

title: Synthesize cards rows for bridged TCGCSV groups with no pokemontcg.io counterpart
description:
After pokedumpster-1x0 the MEP set tile renders in /browse, but clicking it opens an empty set — the 'cards' table has zero rows for set_code='mep' because pokemontcg.io has no upstream MEP set entry. TCGCSV has 83 product rows in group 24451 with enough data to synthesize bare-bones card rows so the binder grid actually populates.

Same shape would apply to any future synthesize-style bridge entry.

Out of scope for pokedumpster-1x0 (which delivered the set-tile bridge); this is the follow-up to make the bridged tile useful.
design:
TCGCSV product fields available per MEP card:
  - product_id  → tcgplayer_product_id (drives printings + prices)
  - name        → 'Meganium - 001' / 'Alakazam - 003 [Staff]' / 'Alakazam - 003 (Pokemon Center Exclusive)'
  - collector_number → '001' / '003' (variant treatments share the number)
  - image_url   → small/large image

Minimum to produce a usable card row:
  - card_id = '{set_code}-{number}' (e.g. 'mep-1', 'mep-3')
  - name    = parse_product_card_name (strips ' - 001' suffix and any trailing parenthetical/staff tag)
  - number, number_sortable
  - image_small / image_large from TCGCSV image_url
  - rarity = NULL (TCGCSV does not carry this)

Implementation likely lives in a new ingest module run during 'pkdump setup' / 'data refresh' after the bridge synthesis step. Idempotent — INSERT OR IGNORE on (card_id) keyed by collector_number per set_code, then variant expansion (now scanning the synthesized set's group via the existing own-group path in pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs:151) creates printings from the same products that justify the cards row.

Bridge entries opt in via a new 'synthesize_cards: true' flag on their entry in data/overrides/tcgcsv_set_bridges.json — SVP doesn't need it (pokemontcg.io provides cards), MEP does.
acceptance_criteria:
- After data refresh: cards table has one row per unique collector_number in TCGCSV group 24451.
- /browse/mep renders a populated binder grid with images.
- Cards picked up from TCGCSV (no upstream pokemontcg.io entry) are marked clearly so a future upstream-arrival merge is mechanical.
- Idempotent: re-running data refresh doesn't duplicate or drift the synthesized rows.
notes: Filed as the follow-up to pokedumpster-1x0. The bridge framework is already in place; this is the cards-population half.

V3 migration adds tcgcsv_products.image_url; import_products now also derives stamp variants so own-group [Staff]/(Prerelease) products resolve correctly. value: Data model is the product. Anything data-shaped (lookups, labels, ranks, enums, derived display metadata) living in API or frontend code is a smell — flag it immediately. The schema is what lets UI tweaks stay simple and lets edge cases (which will surface as the collection is entered in anger) get fixed in one place. Bias toward: define it as a table or seed file, attach an FK, let display code do nothing but render. Examples found in May 2026: variantLabel/variantRank/variantColor/variantTag scattered across TS while the canonical variant list lived in a Rust constant — fixed by moving to shared.sqlite variants table (pokedumpster-mk4).
